cells.tense: You're the one deciding which of the feelings in front of you get kept and which get let go, and you're doing it right now, pen in hand.
cells.verb: gathering the emotional possibilities still live
cells.place: at the point where what you've gathered is finishing itself into something you can hand over
cells.ask: offer one of these possibilities to someone instead of holding all of them open — and notice how it feels when understanding lands between you and neither of you disappears into the other.
cells.core: You can feel what's possible between people — the many directions a moment could go — and you're not scattered by it. You're holding the options and letting them settle into one. That settling is not a loss of the rest; it's what makes any of them real, and you're doing it without going numb to the others.
cells.sheetLine: You gather what could be felt, and you choose which of it gets to become real.

cells.tense: You're already living in a completion that hasn't happened yet — future tense, bracing at a door before it's there.
cells.verb: pulling every feeling that could ever arrive into right now
cells.place: standing in an ending you're forcing to finish ahead of its own timing
cells.ask: keep one ending you're bracing for from moving forward in you — hold it exactly as it is for a day — and notice that transformation moves on its own necessity, and that what you end can be honored without being rushed, and what comes next doesn't need you to feel it before it's here.
cells.core: Every possible feeling between you and everyone is already in the room for you — not as possibility but as demand. You feel the goodbye before it's said, the shift before it happens, the version of this that hasn't arrived. The problem isn't feeling too much; it's that none of it has a floor to stand on, so nothing can finish. You're trying to complete something by staying ahead of it, and that's exactly what keeps it from completing.
cells.sheetLine: You're living in a completion that hasn't happened, and the bracing is what's keeping it open.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you — past tense, the integration done and you not in it.
cells.place: after the completion already happened, not walking through it
cells.ask: let the understanding you already have sit still in you for a moment instead of reaching for the next thing — and notice what it's like when recognition comes without you chasing it, when your own stillness holds both you and the other person in one place.
cells.core: The feelings are still there and you've stopped picking them up. Somewhere back there, gathering what people might feel became too much to do out loud, so you stopped reaching for it — and what's left is a person who can see the possibilities but won't move toward any of them. The integration isn't missing. Your hands are just not on it.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what's possible between people and you've stopped picking any of it up.

cells.tense: You're already deciding which feelings get offered to people and which stay back — present tense, pen down in a room you're still writing.
cells.verb: shaping what people are allowed to feel from you
cells.place: inside a completion you're calling just how things are
cells.ask: name one thing you've already settled about how something between you and someone ends, say it out loud once — and notice what you see in the pattern when it's yours to say, the understanding that was already working showing its shape where you can see it.
cells.core: You're already the one editing what people get to feel from you — what you let show, what you keep warm, what you hold at arm's length. It's working; people feel the shape of you. But you talk about it as though the shape were just how you are, a fact about the room rather than a choice you make. The choosing is running. The claim on it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're already shaping what people feel from you. You just haven't said so.

flags.detail: Too Much and Too Little open identically
